paragraphs: On Sunday, Dad took Lily and Mia to the town stadium. Tom had a football match there with his school team. Next to the stadium, there was a small funfair with a big wheel. The children arrived at one o'clock. The place was very noisy. Dad held three tickets and looked at them. "Which gate is ours?" asked Lily. "Our gate is number three," said Dad. "Please stay with me, girls."

Mia looked at everything. She saw red balloons, music, and a man with a big drum. She walked to a gate, but she mixed up the numbers. It was gate eight, not gate three. When she turned around, Dad and Lily were not there. Mia felt a little afraid, but she stayed calm.

At gate three, Lily said, "Dad, where is Mia?" Dad looked everywhere, and he did not see her. They went to the information desk. Dad spoke to a woman in a green vest. "What does she look like?" asked the woman. "She wears a yellow T-shirt with a blue fish," said Lily. "She has a white bag and white shoes." "She is ten years old." "She is tall for her age."

The woman took a phone and spoke to the helpers at all the gates. After two minutes, a helper at gate eight called back. "A girl in a yellow T-shirt is here," he said. Dad and Lily ran to gate eight. Mia was there. "I mixed up the gates," said Mia. "It is OK," said Dad. He gave her a hug. Then the three of them walked to gate three. They watched Tom play.
text.summary: Dad takes Lily and Mia to Tom's football match at the stadium. Mia mixes up the gates and gets lost, and a helper finds her from her yellow T-shirt.
